title: How a Fridge Works
text: A fridge keeps food cold so it stays fresh for longer. Inside the fridge there is a special liquid in thin pipes. The liquid takes the heat from the food and carries it away. Then the liquid goes to the back, where the heat leaves. This is why the back of a fridge is often warm. A small motor moves the liquid around all day.

text: When I was seven, my father gave me a red bicycle. I was very excited, but I could not ride it. Every evening he ran next to me and held the seat. After two weeks I fell, and I cried a little.
